However, despite their impressive capabilities, ANNs are often limited by their ability to learn efficiently, particularly when dealing with smaller datasets. In this research, we investigate the role of data augmentation techniques in enhancing the neural network's ability to learn and generalize. Our findings reveal that data augmentation can lead to improved learning and generalization capabilities, particularly when certain conditions are met. Furthermore, we identify a specific threshold for the amount of data augmentation required to achieve optimal results, which can vary depending on the size of the dataset. Interestingly, our study shows that using the right amount of data augmentation can even enhance the neural network's ability to learn from smaller datasets, making it comparable to learning from larger datasets. Our proposed method, data augmentation-based learning (DABL), demonstrates that it can achieve similar performance to its baseline counterpart using significantly less data, which is a promising result for practical applications. Finally, we discuss the potential limitations of our method and provide guidance on when data augmentation can be an effective tool for improving neural network performance.
